subject: Vendor invoice submission: portal vs email — sample rows and exception cases
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@papertrailco.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice submission options for PaperTrail — quick question

Hi Sofia & Marissa,

We're getting set up to bill Redwood for the pilot work and want to confirm the preferred channel for submitting invoices. We currently have three routes: (1) upload to your vendor portal, (2) email invoices to billing@papertrailco.com (our AP), or (3) send a CSV batch via SFTP.

Two quick asks: can you confirm which of those Redwood prefers (portal vs email) and whether you require a PO number or PO-stamping for each invoice? Our team is used to email attachments, but if portal upload is required we can prioritize integration.

I've attached our standard invoice template and a small sample CSV.

Thanks — Liam
Liam O'Neill
Finance Lead, PaperTrail Co.
Attachments: sample_invoice_lines.csv (CSV sample), onboarding_form_v2.pdf (PDF)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@papertrailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission options for PaperTrail — quick question

Hi Liam — thanks for the file, that helps. Short answer: we prefer the vendor portal for day-to-day invoice intake because it provides automated validation (PO matching, line-level taxes) and reduces manual touch. We do allow email as a fallback for small invoices or one-off corrections.

Key rules we follow:
- PO is required for any invoice over $5,000. If you don't have a PO, route invoices to billing@redwood-invoices.com (exceptions inbox) and flag the line that requires a PO request.
- Portal preferred for recurring/volume billing and for invoices containing more than 10 line items.
- Email fallback acceptable for single-line invoices under $500 (one-off consulting, expense reimbursements), but these must include a PO if available.
- If sending by email, put the PO number in the subject line and first line of the email body to help auto-route (e.g., "PO 2027-3941 - Invoice 12345").

I've attached our vendor onboarding form and a CSV example with the exact field names we use (see sample_invoice_lines.csv). I'll loop in our procurement tech contact if you decide to integrate via SFTP/API.

Sofia Ivanova
Vendor Onboarding Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: portal_integration_spec.docx (integration spec)

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@papertrailco.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@papertrailco.com
Date: 2027-09-06T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission options for PaperTrail — quick question

Thanks, Sofia — that is clear and aligns with what we expected. A couple follow-ups:
1) Our current template puts tax and discount at the header level — your CSV sample shows those fields per line. Is header-level tax acceptable?
2) For PO-less invoices under $5k we may still need a one-off approval. If we email, who should we expect to see a response from and in what SLA?

I'll have AP try a portal upload this week and report back on any validation failures.

— Liam

On the CSV: we can change to include tax per-line; let us know the required column order and we'll re-export.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-07T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission options for PaperTrail — quick question

Looping in a quick clarification for AP operations: header-level tax is acceptable only if the invoice has a single tax jurisdiction and the tax_total field is supplied. For multi-jurisdiction or per-line tax, use the per-line tax_rate column in CSV. Also:
- PO-stamping: our AP team stamps inbound PDFs with the matched PO if a PO was supplied in the header; otherwise they open an exception ticket.
- Exception SLA: email fallback tickets are triaged within 2 business days; urgent escalations (payment hold) require "PRIORITY: AP ESCALATION" in the subject.

Marissa — can you confirm our recommended subject line template for vendor emails so we can send a short doc to Liam?

Karthik
Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@papertrailco.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-08T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission options for PaperTrail — quick question

Hi Liam — thanks for testing the portal. Two quick next steps and an exemplar subject line:

1) If you upload via portal: choose "Goods & Services" tax profile and attach CSV with columns: invoice_number, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD), po_number, line_description, quantity, unit_price, tax_rate, line_tax_amount, currency, total_line_amount.
2) If you must email: subject should start with PO when available; otherwise use: "Vendor: PaperTrail Co. | INV: <invoice_number> | AMT: <amount>". That helps our parser.

Exemplar: "PO 2027-3941 | Vendor: PaperTrail Co. | INV: 12345 | AMT: 4,250.00"

If portal validation fails for a file, include the portal error report when you email to billing@redwood-invoices.com so AP can process the exception faster. We'll accept header-level tax for single-jurisdiction invoices but prefer per-line tax when multiple tax rates apply.

I'll attach a short one-page "Portal vs Email" checklist after this thread; for now the attachments we referenced are: onboarding_form_v2.pdf, sample_invoice_lines.csv, portal_integration_spec.docx.

Best — Marissa
Vendor Ops & AP Liaison, Redwood Inference
